thesis: Scott Chacon argues that Git, originally designed as Unix plumbing for the Linux kernel, lacks a unified design philosophy and has evolved into a 'Frankenstein' tool that struggles with modern coding agents. He suggests that while the core data storage and transmission protocols should remain unchanged, the user interface requires a complete rethink to accommodate the new ergonomics of AI-assisted coding.
